cover.headline: A sound carbon black franchise carrying a debt-funded detour, priced as if the detour has already paid off
cover.lead: PCBL is India's largest carbon black maker (900 kt, ~6th globally) with a growing specialty-black business and 122 MW of free co-generated power. In Jan-2024 it bought Aquapharm, a phosphonates maker, for ₹3,800 cr, almost all with debt. Two years on, Aquapharm earns ₹162 cr of EBITDA against ₹417 cr before the deal, carbon black EBITDA per tonne fell from ~₹19,200 (FY25) to ~₹14,200 (FY26), net borrowings are ₹4,536 cr (5.0x EBITDA on CARE's measure) and all three rating agencies have a Negative outlook. Q1FY27 was a record, but ~₹70 cr of it was cheap inventory. We forecast EPS of ₹9.2 / 12.3 / 14.3 for FY27-29E, below the street. The street values PCBL on **P/E**; at ₹331.1 the stock trades at 24.9x our Sep-28E EPS. Our **16x** (the stock's own history, re-weighted for today's specialty mix, no premium while ROE trails the cost of equity) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** EV/EBITDA (₹231) and DCF (₹216) agree. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}: leverage makes the range wide.

arguments.h: Carbon black: real scale, borrowed pricing power
arguments.p: Volumes rose from 389 kt (FY21) to 619 kt (FY26) and capacity is now 900 kt. But rubber black is priced off crude through formulas with tyre majors and off Russian and Chinese imports in the spot market. EBITDA per tonne swung from ~₹19,200 (FY25) to ~₹14,200 (FY26) to ₹22,900 in Q1FY27 (incl. ~₹70 cr of inventory gains). Guidance for FY27 is ₹16,500-17,000. Specialty blacks (+23% in Q1) and power are the steady profit pools.

arguments.h: Aquapharm has been a costly mistake so far
arguments.p: ₹3,800 cr was paid for a business that made ₹417 cr of EBITDA in FY23; it made ₹194 cr in FY25 and ₹162 cr in FY26, and the Chemicals segment earned ₹17 cr of operating profit on ₹4,226 cr of assets. Management missed its FY26 target (₹300 cr) by 46% and its ₹75 cr exit-quarter target by 61%; a new CEO arrived in Jul-2026 and declined to repeat it.

arguments.h: Leverage and governance cap the multiple
arguments.p: Debt has barely moved since the deal (₹4,825 cr gross at Mar-26), the Andhra Pradesh plant (Phase I ~₹1,100 cr) will be debt-funded, and we see net debt still ~2.8x EBITDA in FY29E against a Vision 2030 target of below 1x. PCBL also gave ₹35 cr to political parties in FY26 (18% of net profit), holds ₹464 cr of RPSG group-company shares and paid 119% of FY26 EPS as dividend.

arguments.h: The price assumes Vision 2030 will be delivered
arguments.p: At ₹331.1, PCBL trades at 26.9x our FY28E EPS. Its forward P/E was 9.9x in the commodity years (2021-23) and 28.4x after the Aquapharm deal; the house median since Apr-2021 (ex-FY26) is 13.7x. The gap is the market paying for ₹4,000 cr of FY30 EBITDA, including ₹1,400 cr from battery materials that have no revenue yet. Upside needs proof, not promises.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much of Q1's ~₹70 cr inventory gain reverses (management: ₹40-50 cr) and whether volumes dip as guided.
Aquapharm: the new CEO's plan, promised for the next call; oil & gas recovery; green-chelate approvals with P&G, Reckitt and Henkel.
Capex decisions: coal-tar distillation (approval expected in Q2FY27) and the Andhra Pradesh greenfield (Phase I 150 kt, ~₹1,100 cr), and how they are funded.
Credit: CRISIL's downgrade trigger is debt/EBITDA above 3-3.25x; CARE's is debt/PBILDT above 4x (5.0x in FY26).
Nanovace: customer sampling of nano-silicon from Aug-2026; management expects commercial volumes in FY28.

sections.title: What PCBL does: burns heavy oil into carbon black, sells the waste heat as power, and owns a water-chemicals maker

blocks.p: Carbon black is a fine black powder made by burning heavy oil (carbon black feedstock, CBFS, a by-product of oil refining) with too little air. About 60% of the world's carbon black goes into tyres, where it gives rubber strength and wear resistance; the rest goes into belts, hoses and other rubber goods ("performance" grades) and, as "specialty" blacks, into plastics, inks, paints, cables and battery electrodes. PCBL (formerly Phillips Carbon Black, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka group) has five carbon black plants (Durgapur, Mundra, Palej, Kochi and Chennai) with 900 kt of capacity, of which 132 kt is specialty. ~57% of its carbon black goes to tyre makers, mostly on formula contracts that pass crude-linked feedstock costs through with a one-month or one-quarter lag; about a third of volume is sold spot. Around 38-40% of volume is exported. The hot tail gas from the reactors runs 122 MW of power plants: PCBL uses what it needs and sells the rest to the grid.

Since Jan-2024 PCBL also owns **Aquapharm** (Specialty & Solutions): India's largest and the world's third-largest phosphonate maker (phosphonates stop scale and corrosion in water systems and are used in detergents), plus oil-field chemicals, polymers and "green chelates" (biodegradable replacements for phosphonates in detergents). It has plants at Mahad and Pirangut (Maharashtra), Jeddah and Texas, 167 kt of capacity and sells ~83% outside India (North America ~50%). The third leg, **battery materials** (Nanovace nano-silicon anodes, super-conductive carbons, acetylene black), is still at pilot stage.

blocks.callout: **So what:** PCBL is three businesses with very different quality. Rubber black is a scale commodity whose spread is set by crude and imports; specialty blacks and free power are genuinely good profit pools; Aquapharm is a niche specialty-chemicals franchise that has earned almost nothing on the ₹4,226 cr of assets PCBL now carries for it. The battery business is an option, not yet a business.

sections.title: Industry: steady demand, but price is set by crude, Russia and Indian overcapacity

blocks.p: Global demand for rubber black is ~13.6 mn t a year, growing ~3-4% with tyre output; specialty blacks are ~1.1 mn t, growing 4-5% (company). India has become a net exporter: exports rose 12% in FY26 to 4.44 lakh t while imports fell 11% to 1.30 lakh t (CARE). The problem for Indian producers has been price, not demand. After EU sanctions, Russian carbon black (made from cheap Russian feedstock) was diverted to India and South-East Asia, Indian capacity grew faster than local demand, and US tariffs (an effective ~20% on PCBL's ~₹350 cr of US sales, ~₹70 cr of EBITDA a year in Oct-2025) closed one outlet. In 2026 the picture improved: the India-US deal lowered tariffs, the India-EU FTA will remove the 4.5% EU duty on Indian tyres, and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries cut Russian carbon black imports into India by ~40% in Jan-Jun 2026 while dearer Chinese material (~$1.3/kg vs ~$1.0/kg) filled the gap.

sections.title: Carbon black: volumes grow every year; EBITDA per tonne is the whole story, and it swings ±25%

blocks.p: Carbon black is ~80% of PCBL's revenue. Volume has been the easy part: 389 kt in FY21, 619 kt in FY26 (+10% a year) and 153.5 kt in Q1FY27 (flat YoY by choice: PCBL cut low-margin exports when freight jumped and sold more in India). Profit per tonne is the hard part. On our basis (carbon black and power EBITDA ÷ tonnes), it rose from ~₹13,300 (FY21) to ~₹19,300 (FY24) as specialty mix and the new Chennai plant helped, held in FY25, then fell to ~₹14,234 in FY26 as Russian imports and Indian overcapacity crushed spot prices (company basis: ₹14,939). Q1FY27 printed ₹22,900 on the company basis, but ~₹70 cr (~₹4,500/t) was low-cost inventory and the power price jumped 47%; ICICI Direct puts the adjusted figure at ₹18,430.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** guidance of ₹16,500-17,000/t for FY27 (+14-15%) is credible because Q1 is banked, but it relies on the Russian squeeze lasting and on ₹200-250 cr of cost savings that have not yet shown up. We model ₹16,400 / 17,200 / 17,700 per tonne on the Screener basis (≈₹500/t below the company's basis) and volumes of 650 / 696 / 737 kt for FY27-29E, below management's 'high single-digit' growth. Management's ₹24,000-25,000/t five-year aspiration would need the specialty and battery mix of Vision 2030; its earlier ₹20-22/kg aspiration (FY25) was followed by ₹14.9/kg.

sections.title: Aquapharm: ₹3,800 cr for ₹417 cr of EBITDA that has become ₹162 cr

blocks.p: PCBL agreed to buy 100% of Aquapharm Chemicals on 28-Nov-2023 for ₹3,800 cr, about 9x the ₹417 cr of EBITDA Aquapharm made in FY23 on revenue of ₹2,045 cr (a 20% margin). The deal closed in Jan-2024 and was "majorly debt funded" (CARE). Since then the business has shrunk: revenue was ₹1,420 cr in FY25 and ₹1,443 cr in FY26, EBITDA ₹194 cr (13.7%) and ₹162 cr (11.2%). After ₹143 cr of depreciation and amortisation (including amortisation of the ₹2,310 cr of customer, product and IP intangibles created by the deal), the Chemicals segment made a profit before interest and tax of ₹17 cr in FY26 on ₹4,226 cr of segment assets, a fraction of the interest on the debt raised to buy it. Causes: US oil & gas drilling slowed (oil & gas volume −19% in FY26, −35% YoY in Q1FY27), European detergent makers are moving from phosphonates to green chelates, raw materials (yellow phosphorus, acrylic acid) and freight jumped with the West Asia conflict, and low utilisation turned fixed costs into losses.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** on today's numbers PCBL overpaid. ₹3,800 cr of mostly borrowed money now earns ~₹160 cr of EBITDA, a ~4% pre-tax cash return, well below the ~8-9% interest it pays. Aquapharm is a real franchise (world #3 in phosphonates, long relationships with P&G, Henkel and Reckitt, plants in the US and Saudi Arabia), and green chelates are an opportunity. But we need evidence before modelling a recovery: we assume revenue +8% / +10% / +10% and EBITDA margins of 11.5% / 12.5% / 13.5% for FY27-29E (EBITDA ₹{{F.seg.aq.adjEbitda.0|num}} / {{F.seg.aq.adjEbitda.1|num}} / {{F.seg.aq.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr), still well short of the ₹417 cr it made before the deal and of management's ₹75 cr a quarter.

sections.title: Vision 2030 asks for 3x EBITDA in five years; the track record says haircut it heavily

blocks.p: At the RPSG Investor Day (8-Sep-2025) PCBL promised to double revenue to ~₹16,000 cr, triple EBITDA to ~₹4,000 cr and multiply profit 5x by FY30 from FY25, with specialty products rising from 28% to 63% of EBITDA and net debt falling from 3.6x to below 1x EBITDA. The bridge: ₹150 cr from cost savings, ₹400 cr from carbon black capacity (Tamil Nadu brownfield, Andhra Pradesh greenfield), ₹100 cr from specialty blacks, ₹600 cr from Aquapharm and ₹1,400 cr from battery materials (super-conductive carbons, nano-silicon, acetylene black). The CFO reaffirmed it in Apr-2026. In the year since, FY26 EBITDA fell 22%, Aquapharm missed its targets and battery revenue is still nil. Our FY29E EBITDA is ₹{{F.ebitda.2|num}} cr, ~61% below the FY30 target a year earlier.

blocks.p: **Battery materials, honestly.** Nanovace (PCBL 51%, in a joint venture with Kindia of Australia) holds a US process patent for making nano-silicon for lithium-ion anodes. Its 80-tonne pilot plant at Palej received consent to operate in Jul-2026 and was due to start sampling to battery makers in Aug-2026; management expects qualification within the year and commercial volumes in FY28, and CRISIL was told margins could exceed 30%. Alongside, a 1,000 tpa super-conductive black line has started and a 4,000 tpa acetylene black plant is in engineering. These are good businesses to be in, but qualification with cell makers typically takes years, the competition (Chinese and Western silicon-anode start-ups) is well funded, and no customer, price or capacity plan has been disclosed. We put nothing in our forecasts, even in the bull case: any battery-materials revenue would be upside to all three scenarios.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** management has a habit of setting ambitious numbers (₹20-22/kg EBITDA in carbon black, ₹300 cr for Aquapharm in FY26, ₹4,000 cr of EBITDA by FY30) and keeping them after the year turns out badly. We give credit for what is in its control (volume growth, specialty lines, cost savings) and none yet for battery materials.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (filings, calls, rating rationales to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** PCBL has a **cost-and-scale position** in carbon black (largest Indian producer, port-side plants, by-product power) and a **genuine specialty-black business**. That is enough to win volume and survive downturns. It is **not** enough to set prices: in rubber black the spread is decided by crude, by Russian and Chinese imports and by Indian rivals' spare capacity, which is why EBITDA per tonne fell 26% in FY26. Aquapharm has a franchise but has not shown it can earn its cost of capital under PCBL. ROE of 5% (FY26) and ~11-12% in our FY28-29E is the honest scorecard: no moat premium.

sections.title: Quarters: a record Q1FY27, but about ₹70 cr of it came from cheap inventory

blocks.p: Quarterly EBITDA slid from ₹358-364 cr in H1FY25 to a low of ₹215 cr in Q3FY26 as carbon black spreads fell and Aquapharm weakened. Q1FY27 jumped to ₹396 cr (16% margin): crude rose from $78 to $97 a barrel, PCBL sold its low-cost inventory at new, higher prices (~₹70 cr of gains, says the CFO), took spot-price premiums on about a third of its volume and got ₹5.39 per unit for surplus power (₹3.66 in Q4FY26). Management itself warned that ₹40-50 cr of the inventory benefit reverses in Q2FY27 and that customers were buying cautiously. Underlying Q1 EBITDA was closer to ₹326-340 cr (ICICI Securities, Nuvama), still the best quarter in a year.

Quarterly net profit: from ₹2 cr (Q3FY26) to ₹155 cr

blocks.callout: **So what:** do not annualise Q1FY27. Strip out the inventory gain and the run-rate is ~₹1,300-1,350 cr of EBITDA a year, and Q2FY27 (results due by mid-November 2026) carries the reversal plus softer volumes. Our FY27E EBITDA of {{F.ebitda.0|num}} cr assumes ~₹280 cr a quarter for Q2-Q4.

sections.title: Revenue tripled since FY21 but profit is lower: an acquisition bought sales, not earnings

blocks.p: PCBL's revenue rose from ₹2,660 cr in FY21 to ₹8,404 cr in FY25: carbon black prices followed crude up in FY22-23, volumes grew from 389 kt to 596 kt, and Aquapharm (acquired in Jan-2024) added ~₹1,400 cr a year. EBITDA rose from ₹517 cr to ₹1,337 cr. Then FY26 went wrong: carbon black realisations fell (Russian imports, Indian overcapacity, US tariffs), EBITDA dropped 22% to ₹1,043 cr and net profit more than halved to ₹198 cr (EPS ₹5.0, from ₹13.0 in FY24). Below EBITDA, the acquisition changed the cost structure: interest went from ₹34 cr (FY21) to ₹423 cr and depreciation from ₹110 cr to ₹373 cr, together 76% of FY26 EBITDA.

pair.title: Revenue: ₹8,189 cr in FY26, three times FY21
EBITDA: ₹1,337 cr peak (FY25), back to ₹1,043 cr
Interest and depreciation now absorb three-quarters of EBITDA
Net profit: ₹198 cr in FY26, below FY19
EBITDA margin: 12-19%, it moves with crude

blocks.callout: **Our view:** PCBL used to be a high-return commodity business: ROCE of 16-25% in FY19-FY23 with little debt. Over FY21-26 it generated ₹4,620 cr of operating cash, spent ₹3,354 cr on plants and ₹3,708 cr on Aquapharm, and borrowed the difference. ROCE is now ~8%, below the ~11% cost of capital. A margin percentage tells you little here (revenue swings with crude); the numbers that matter are carbon black EBITDA per tonne and Aquapharm's EBITDA, covered in their own chapters.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but inventory swings, deal accounting and donations sit in the numbers

bullets: **Inventory gains and losses.** Formula pricing passes crude through with a lag, so rising crude creates gains on cheap stock and falling crude creates losses. Q1FY27 included ~₹70 cr of gains (CFO), ₹40-50 cr of which he expected to reverse in Q2FY27; FY26 margins were hurt the other way.

**Working capital flatters FY26 cash.** Operating cash flow of ₹1,576 cr included a ₹529 cr release of working capital as crude fell; Q1FY27 rebuilt inventory (₹117 cr increase) as crude rose. Expect much of that release to reverse.

**Deal accounting.** The Aquapharm purchase created ₹1,161 cr of goodwill and ~₹2,310 cr of customer, product and IP intangibles. Their amortisation inflates Chemicals D&A (₹143 cr in FY26) and depresses EPS by a non-cash charge. In FY25 a ₹555 cr goodwill impairment was booked as an exceptional item and exactly offset by a ₹554 cr deferred-tax reversal from merging Aquapharm into Advaya Chemical: a large write-down that left no trace in profit.

**Political donations in operating costs.** "Subscriptions and donations" include ₹35 cr (FY26) and ₹44.5 cr (FY25) of contributions under Section 182 of the Companies Act, booked in other expenses, i.e. inside EBITDA (3% of FY26 EBITDA, 18% of net profit).

**Power is a transfer-price profit.** The Power segment's ₹239 cr PBIT includes captive power sold to the carbon black plants at the price of grid power (₹131 cr of inter-segment revenue). It is real value, but the segment split depends on that price.
**Exceptional and one-off items.** FY26: −₹25 cr for the new labour codes. FY27: a ₹40-45 cr US tariff refund was expected (accounting not decided); we exclude it.

**Investments are group-company shares.** The ₹464 cr shown as investments (CESC ₹253 cr, RPSG Ventures, Spencer's and unquoted group firms) is not liquid treasury; their fair-value changes go through OCI (−₹42 cr in FY26).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** S.R. Batliboi & Co. gave a clean opinion (key audit matters: revenue recognition, contingencies and the goodwill/intangible impairment test). We see no sign of manipulation, but reported profit swings with crude-driven inventory effects, is reduced by non-cash deal amortisation, and carries political donations inside operating costs. CFO/EBITDA was 151% in FY26 and 57% in FY25: the working-capital swing, not a change in quality.

sections.title: Net debt: ~₹4,500 cr, five times EBITDA, and it stopped falling once capex resumes

blocks.p: Before Aquapharm, PCBL had almost no net debt (₹39 cr at Mar-22). Borrowings jumped from ₹1,029 cr (Mar-23) to ₹4,983 cr (Mar-24) to fund the ₹3,800 cr purchase, and have stayed there: ₹5,571 cr at Mar-25 and ₹4,989 cr at Mar-26 including leases. FY26 was a good cash year (operating cash ₹1,576 cr, helped by ₹529 cr of working-capital release as crude fell), the promoters paid ₹336 cr for their warrants, and the company cut net borrowings by ₹454 cr to ₹4,536 cr. Even so, debt was 5.0x EBITDA (CARE), above every agency's comfort level. Note that Screener's "investments" (₹464 cr) are shares of RPSG group companies (CESC ₹253 cr and unquoted group entities), not cash.

sections.title: Ownership: the Goenka group holds 53%, Indian institutions are buying, foreign funds are not

blocks.p: The RP-Sanjiv Goenka group owns 53.38% (Jun-2026), almost all through Rainbow Investments (47.4%); nothing is pledged, and 1.6 cr shares from the ₹280 warrant conversion are locked in. Domestic institutions own 11.27% (mutual funds 5.62%, insurers 5.56%), up from ~6% in early 2024; foreign investors own only 5.79% (7.1% in Dec-2023). About 275,000 shareholders hold the rest; small individuals alone own 21.39%.

sections.title: Our forecasts: EPS recovers to ₹{{F.eps.2|n1}} by FY29E, 20-30% below the street

blocks.p: We model the two businesses the way management reports them. **Carbon black (incl. power)** = tonnes × realisation for revenue and tonnes × EBITDA per tonne for profit; corporate costs and Nanovace development sit inside it. **Aquapharm** = revenue growth × EBITDA margin. FY27E: carbon black volume +5% (Q1 flat, Q2 soft by management's own warning; guidance 'high single digit'), realisation ₹125/kg, EBITDA/t ₹16,400 on our basis (≈₹16,900 on the company's, inside the ₹16,500-17,000 guidance); Aquapharm +8% at 11.5%. FY28-29E: volume +7% / +6% (900 kt is ~82% used by FY29E; Andhra Pradesh adds from FY30), EBITDA/t ₹17,200 / ₹17,700, Aquapharm 12.5% / 13.5%. Capex ₹300 / 800 / 900 cr, interest ₹370 / 355 / 360 cr, tax 25%, payout 50%. Every input is on the Excel model's Assumptions sheet, which recalculates this report's target.

sections.title: The street: four Holds or worse and one Buy; average target ~₹352

blocks.p: Five houses had calls standing on 30-Sep-2026: Prabhudas Lilladher BUY ₹391 (8-Sep, upgraded from Accumulate on the Russian import squeeze; 25x FY28E EPS of ₹15.5), ICICI Direct HOLD ₹350 (20x FY28E), Nuvama HOLD ₹350, IDBI Capital HOLD ₹352 and ICICI Securities REDUCE ₹315 (20x FY27-28E). The average, ~₹352, is +6% vs the 30-Sep price. Every house that discloses a method uses P/E. The cautious houses point to Q1's inventory gains, a likely Q2 dip and Aquapharm; the bull (PL) argues that guidance of ~₹17,000/t is conservative if Russian supply stays short. Targets fell from ₹474 (PL, Sep-2025) to ₹270-310 (May-2026) and recovered after Q1FY27.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good core business, a poor acquisition, a stretched balance sheet and a full price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest carbon black maker (900 kt, port-side plants, 40% exported), a fast-growing specialty-black line, 122 MW of by-product power, the world's #3 phosphonate maker (Aquapharm) and an early-stage battery-materials option, run by the RP-Sanjiv Goenka group.

**What you are paying:** 26.9x our FY28E EPS and 12.2x FY28E EV/EBITDA for a company with ROE of 5% (FY26) rising to ~12% (FY29E), net debt of ~4x EBITDA, three Negative rating outlooks and a record of missing its own targets.
